The same onset of the rains reads differently with what she believes of him. This is a specific and true point.

The two disagree about what gossip does: the Kural welcomes it (யாம்வேண்டும் கௌவை எடுக்கும்இவ் வூர்), and 302 fears it has kept him away (பிரியா நண்பினர் இருவரும் என்னும் அலரதற்கு அஞ்சினன் கொல்லோ). The snapping-waist conceit is shared (சிறிதவள் செல்வாள் இறும் என்று அஞ்சி; நுகப்பிற்கு நல்ல படாஅ பறை). The same word carries both: கௌவை ஆகின்றது ஐய நின் நட்பே and யாம்வேண்டும் கௌவை. The colophon of 354 is the friend pressing for marriage (வரைவு கடாயது). Told to the man directly, the talk becomes a reproach, where in the Kural it is welcomed. The Kural speaker's identity comes from commentary, but the contrast in how the talk is aimed stands on the Tamil.

Both end the land's loneliness with the same noun: மலர்ந்த ஞாலம் புலம்புபுறக் கொடுப்ப as a sign before he comes (உவக்காண் தோன்றும்), and புலம்பு தீர்ந்து இனிய ஆயின புறவே ... யாம் வந்தமாறே in the man's own mouth, as caused by his coming. The shift from sign to claimed effect is specific and true.

Paripadal 5 does refuse wealth and pleasure (பொருளும் பொன்னும் போகமும் அல்ல ... அருளும் அன்பும் அறனும்). The 'festive versus moral' opposition overstates the difference between the two prayers.

Its 'desire' comes from reading சிறுமை as lust, which is a commentator's gloss, so the tension with 440's காதல காதல் அறியாமை உய்க்கிற்பின் rests on that gloss. The teaches ('Removing and hiding are different programmes') is too thin to teach anything.

The word and the organ match: கண்ணே காமம் கரப்பு அரியவ்வே and கரப்பினும் கையிகந்து ஒல்லாநின் உண்கண். Natrinai sorts the signs as the teaches says: தொடி பழி மறைத்தலின் தோள் உய்ந்தனவே, the hair excused by play (ஆயமோடு ஆடலின்), and the eyes that cannot hide. The concealment the couplet takes for granted is set out part by part.
links.text_issue: 23 line 3 (இடிப்பு மெய்யது ஒன்று உடைத்தே) is hard.

links.reason: The herdsmen's flute at the rainy evening is in both (குழல் தொடங்கினரே கோவலர்; கோவலர் கொன்றைஅம் தீம் குழல் மன்றுதோறு இயம்ப உயிர் செல). But it is a stock mullai sign, and the poems are not matched 'sound for sound': 371 has lightning, rain and slipping bangles, while 364 has bells and the north wind. The 'shared code' reading of the teaches is the shared convention in grander words.

The Innaa's first item (பொருளுணர்வார் இல்வழிப் பாட்டுரைத்தல்) agrees with the Kural's அங்கணத்துள் உக்க அமிழ்தற்றால் ... அல்லார்முன் கோட்டி கொளல. But the Innaa simply lists four unrelated painful things. Reading its first and last lines (பொருளில்லார் வண்மை) as a designed pair, a gift wasted on both sides, rests only on the wordplay on பொருள். The Kural's தங்கணத்தார் அல்லார் is also not the same as 'those who do not grasp the meaning'.

In 286 the hill lord is the grammatical agent of the loss: நன்மலை நாடன் புகரின்று நயந்தனன் போலும் கவரும் ... என் மாமைக் கவினே, and போலும் can be ironic. So 'the waste of her beauty is never his fault in her own mouth' fits the Kural (உள்ளுவன் மன் ... கள்ளம் பிறவோ பசப்பு) but is contradicted or at best strained by 286. The agreement depends on reading போலும் as exculpation.

Both tie the drinking order to the order of battle: 292's man stops the king's toddy and will not wait for his turn (என்முறை வருக என்னான்), so he will hold the army, and 298's warrior, once given the dregs (கலங்கல் தருமே), complains the king does not say நீ முந்து. The pairing shows that precedence at the feast stood for precedence in battle. Both verses are flagged uncertain, so the readings carry some risk.

poems.note: Bees at the kaanthal give only one match (bee to lover at the flower); the arrival is stated outright (நாடனும் வந்தான்).
The bull's tossing the garland into her hair is the plot itself, not a side image.
Lines 1 and 4 are lost; nothing can be tested.

iraicchi.act: the young deer frolics with its mate in the rain
iraicchi.sense: the pair rejoicing together in the season tells the waiting woman her lover is about to come, which consoles her

poems.note: The scene is mapped onto a dance performance, not onto the love situation.
Line 3 (பாசம்பட்டு ஓடும்) is hard; no single implication for the lovers can be fixed.
The bee's joyful singing is sound and mood; the contrast with the man who left is not drawn by an act.
The parrot is the addressed messenger, so it cannot be struck.
The peacock is joined to her openly by நின்னே போல.

iraicchi.act: the bee frolics coupling in flower after flower (பூ அங்கண் புணர்ந்து ஆடி)
iraicchi.sense: it points to the husband's roaming among many women, which the poem then charges him with

poems.note: The lotus opening is likened openly (போல) to the smiling wife.
Herons feeding on the fat fish stranded when the water receded match the man and the girl he consumed and left; the stranded fish and her helplessness give the second pair.
The shark that tore the net is the literal reason the men are away.
The neythal trampled by the heron is an open simile (போல).

iraicchi.act: the monkey leaps from the sweet mango to take the pleasure of the tall jackfruit
iraicchi.sense: the hill lord too may leave her for another delight, so she doubts he will keep his sweet words

poems.note: The cocks' fight is an open simile (போல) for her illness.
Line 1 and most of line 2 are lost.
The anril calling at the yard suggests longing, but the poem's stated sense is too thin to fix what it implies.

iraicchi.act: the wild cow, loving its calf, yields milk as the monkey strokes her udder
iraicchi.sense: in a land of such tender care the lovers cannot part, so the speaker trusts the bond

iraicchi.act: the peacock takes the millet the hill girl guards
iraicchi.sense: the man comes by stealth at midnight to take what her people guard, and she fears the risk to him

iraicchi.act: the milch cows go back toward their calves at evening
iraicchi.sense: the cows return to their own at dusk while he does not return to her, which is why she says she will not survive

poems.note: The buffalo-drivers are likened openly to warriors (மள்ளரின்); no device.
The moon is set against her brow openly (எமதும் உண்டு ஓர் மதிநாட் திங்கள்).

iraicchi.act: the birds snatch the fish while the women sit guarding it
iraicchi.sense: while she kept watch the shore lord took and enjoyed her beauty (நுகர்வனன் உண்டான் நலம்)

poems.note: Line 4 comes close to stating the parallel, which strains condition 3.
அதனால் makes the resting creatures the stated reason for the hour; the end of the poem is lost.
